title: Counting coins by grouping them
examples: How do I count coins quickly?
How much are four coins of five?
Which coins should I count first?

explain.say: Imagine a pile of coins. Counting them one by one is easy to mix up. Here is a smarter way: group them! Look at the board. Each group is one coin worth five, and there are four coins.
Coins worth five? Count in fives! Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. Four coins of five make twenty. Tap each coin as you count. Can you do it with me?
Now three coins worth ten each. Count in tens: ten, twenty, thirty. Thirty altogether! Counting the big coins first makes it quick. Which is worth more, a ten or a five?
Now five coins worth two. Count in twos: two, four, six, eight, ten. That is ten! Sort your coins into piles of the same kind first, then skip count each pile.

Here is the whole plan: sort the coins, start with the biggest, skip count each pile, then put the piles together. Brilliant! Your brain learns in its own way, and lots of brilliant people learn like this.

faq.q: How do I count coins quickly?
faq.a: Sort them into piles of the same kind, then skip count each pile. Coins worth five? Count in fives.

faq.q: Why start with the biggest coins?
faq.a: Big numbers first means fewer steps when you add the small ones on. Count the tens, then count on with fives, twos and ones.
asks: Which coins do I count first?

faq.q: How do I count different coins together?
faq.a: Count one pile at a time, then put the totals together. Thirty from the tens and ten from the twos makes forty.
asks: How do I add up mixed coins?

faq.a: It depends on your country. Many places have coins worth 1, 2, 5 and 10, like rupees in India, pence in the UK, or cents in many other countries.
asks: Which coins does my country have?

faq.q: How can I practise with money?
faq.a: Play shop at home with real or toy coins. A teacher or grown-up can give you prices to pay.

facts: Coins in many countries come in values like 1, 2, 5 and 10, so skip counting in 2s, 5s and 10s helps you count money.

quiz.say: How much are 3 coins worth 10 each?
quiz.why: Count in tens: ten, twenty, thirty.

wrong.1: 13 is ten and three added. Each coin is worth ten.
wrong.2: Three is how many coins, not how much they are worth.

quiz.say: You have coins worth 5. Which way should you count them?
quiz.why: Each coin is worth five, so count in fives.

wrong.1: Counting in ones counts the coins, not their value.
wrong.2: Each coin is worth five, not ten.
